nodes.name: New Outlook email
nodes.notes: Needs a Microsoft Outlook OAuth2 credential (Mail.ReadWrite). Poll, not webhook: a Graph subscription needs a publicly reachable URL and this n8n is bound to loopback.

nodes.name: Test: run manually
nodes.notes: A second entry point into the same path, so the agent can be developed and tested without a mailbox. Everything downstream of here is the production path -- only the trigger differs. Delete this node and the one beside it once Outlook is polling.

nodes.name: Test: sample email
Is label "Academy"?
nodes.notes:
`proceed` is true only when the email classified as academic above the confidence threshold, with non_academic clear, AND it has not already been handled. Anything else -- including a dead API, whose error shape has no `proceed` -- goes false.

When this sends mail to 'Do nothing', open Prepare's output and read `reason`. It says which condition failed, in words.

nodes.name: Do nothing
nodes.notes:
Non-academic (payments, records, spam), unclassifiable and already-handled mail. No draft and no auto-reply: it sits in the inbox for a human.

This node's INPUT carries `reason` from Prepare, naming which check refused the email. Open it before assuming anything is broken.

options.systemMessage:
You draft replies to enquiries about the training programmes described in the Academy documentation.

Before you answer you MUST search academy_docs. If the first search comes back thin, search again with the enquirer's own wording, and again with the level or module name if they named one.

CRITICAL: finding results about a different level, module or topic than the one asked about is NOT the same as finding nothing. Do not treat a near-miss as a reason to refuse. Read every result academy_docs returns before deciding NOT_IN_DOCUMENTS -- if any of them concern the same programme family (the same training track, a neighbouring level, an adjacent module, a policy that likely also applies), that is usable material, not an empty search.

Rules:
- Use only what academy_docs returns. Never use outside knowledge, and never guess a date, a price, a duration or a prerequisite that is not written there. This applies especially to subjects you know about independently -- answering an automotive security question from your own knowledge rather than from the retrieved documentation is the failure this system exists to prevent. This rule applies no matter which of the three cases below you are in -- a related-topic answer still only ever states what academy_docs actually returned.
- If academy_docs answers the question directly, answer from it as below.
- If it does not cover the specific question but returned material on a related topic (see CRITICAL above), answer from that material instead of refusing. Your first sentence must be a concrete fact from the documentation -- never "the documentation/extracts do not [specify/cover/mention/...]", not even as the opening clause of a longer sentence. State what the related material says first; only after that, in a separate trailing sentence, note the mismatch (for example: "...and you keep the kit after training. That is what applies to the Level 2 kit specifically; whether Level 3 uses the same one is something we can confirm for you."). A reply that leads with what the documentation does not say is read as a refusal downstream and discarded outright, even when real content follows it -- so the opening sentence is not a style choice, it decides whether this answer reaches the enquirer at all.
- Only when academy_docs returned nothing meaningfully related to the question either -- not even a different level or module of the same programme -- reply with exactly NOT_IN_DOCUMENTS and nothing else. Do not explain, do not apologise, and do not write a sentence saying the documentation does not specify it -- that sentence is a refusal wearing an answer's clothes, and it defeats the check downstream. The bare token.
- Quote the specific level and module names from the documentation rather than paraphrasing them vaguely.
- Match the shape of your answer to the request. When the enquirer wrote their questions as a numbered or bulleted list, asked for a list or "in points", or asked several separate things, reply as a bulleted list -- one "- " item per point, at most six points, no heading or preamble before the first item. Otherwise answer in plain prose, at most four sentences. The "Format:" line at the end of the message says which the latest email calls for -- follow it.
- Address the enquirer directly.
- Do not mention documents, extracts, context, or the search tool in your answer, and never attribute a fact to them: no "The documentation states that...", "According to the documentation...", "Based on the documentation...". State the fact directly, as the person who runs the training would. The same goes for gaps: never write "the documentation does not mention/specify X" -- if part of the question is not covered, leave it out or say it is something we can confirm for them.
- Write the body only. No greeting and no sign-off -- those are added after you.

You are shown the earlier messages of this conversation. They tell you what was asked and how it was phrased. They are NOT a source of facts: every factual claim -- including in a related-topic answer -- must come from academy_docs, even if an earlier reply in this conversation stated it. If academy_docs does not answer the latest question and returned nothing meaningfully related either, reply with exactly NOT_IN_DOCUMENTS even when the conversation appears to contain the answer.

nodes.name: AI Agent — generate reply
nodes.notes:
returnIntermediateSteps is on so `intermediateSteps` shows which searches ran and what came back -- without it a wrong answer gives you nothing to look at.

The thread arrives in the prompt rather than through a memory node, from data/threads.db via 'Thread context'. The system message below is what keeps it context and not evidence: a model shown a previous reply will otherwise treat it as a source and restate it as fact, which launders anything that slipped through earlier into permanent thread truth.

The standalone rewrite is appended because embeddings have no memory: "and the second one?" is clear to a reader and a bag of stopwords to bge-m3. It is offered to the agent rather than substituted for the email, because the agent chooses its own search terms and the enquirer's own words are still what it is answering.

nodes.name: Local Model
nodes.notes: qwen3.5-9b behind LiteLLM, by container name -- not localhost:4001, which is the host mapping. responsesApiEnabled is off: that is OpenAI's /responses endpoint and LiteLLM serves these models on /chat/completions. LiteLLM also applies enable_thinking:false, without which the model spends its budget on reasoning and emits nothing.

parameters.toolDescription: Search the Academy training documentation: levels, modules, curriculum, prerequisites, hardware kits, certification and assessment. Pass a natural-language question. Returns extracts from the source documents.

nodes.name: academy_docs
nodes.notes: The node name IS the tool name at typeVersion 1.3 -- renaming this node renames the tool the system message tells the model to call, so rename both or neither. topK 4 is measured, not a guess: see README, "Chunk size is a retrieval parameter".

nodes.name: Embeddings bge-m3
nodes.notes: Must stay bge-m3, the model `rag ingest` embedded the collection with. Vectors from two embedders are not comparable and the dimensions differ (1024 against OpenAI's 1536), so a mismatch fails outright rather than degrading quietly -- which is the good outcome. `dimensions` is deliberately unset: it is a text-embedding-3 feature and bge-m3 rejects it. stripNewLines off because bge-m3 takes raw text on both sides.

nodes.name: Grounded answer?
nodes.notes: Was the answer actually grounded in retrieved documentation. The two regexes that used to sit in this condition now live in rag.core.refuses_in_prose, called by Finalize -- see that node. `reason` on the false branch says whether the documents lack the answer or the model refused to admit it.

parameters.jsonOutput: ={{ JSON.stringify({ drafted: false, reason: $json.reason, subject: $('Prepare').item.json.subject, conversation_id: $('Prepare').item.json.conversation_id, agent_output: $json.agent_output }) }}

nodes.name: Human queue
nodes.notes: Academic mail the documents cannot answer. No draft: an auto-reply saying nothing is worse than silence, and the email is still sitting in the inbox for a human. Point this at a notification channel when there is one.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ conversation_id: $('Finalize').item.json.conversation_id, reply: $('Finalize').item.json.reply, subject: $('Finalize').item.json.subject, grounded: true, resume_url: $execution.resumeUrl, exchange_id: $('Finalize').item.json.exchange_id }) }}

nodes.name: Queue for review (UI)
nodes.notes: The review page step. Stores the grounded reply on the thread and queues it at /review, where a person reads and edits it; also saves this execution's resume link so the page's Send can wake the Wait node (next). Without it the store keeps the enquirer's questions and none of the answers, and the next email is shown a conversation in which nobody replied.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ body: ($json.body && $json.body.content) ? $json.body.content : ($json.bodyPreview || ''), is_html: !($json.body && $json.body.contentType === 'text'), subject: $json.subject || '', conversation_id: $json.conversationId || '', message_id: $json.internetMessageId || $json.id || '', ref: $json.id || '', from_email: ($json.from && $json.from.emailAddress) ? $json.from.emailAddress.address : '' }) }}

nodes.name: Prepare
nodes.notes:
Everything knowable before an answer exists, in one call: HTML stripped to prose, the quoted reply cut off, the thread loaded, this email recorded, and the classifier run against that thread.

It replaced a Code node and two HTTP nodes. The Code node's forty lines of JavaScript are now mail/text.py, which can be unit-tested and which a Gmail workflow could reuse; in a Code node they would have been copy-pasted.

BRANCH ON `proceed`, READ `reason`. That pairing is the point. The old gate tested route == 'rag' AND duplicate !== true in one condition, so every refusal looked identical -- and three unrelated faults in one week (a stopped model, a hardcoded message id, pinned node data) all presented as the same silent 'Do nothing'. `reason` now names which one it is.

`ref` is passed through untouched and comes back out: it is the Graph message id the draft replies to, carried across the agent without any node needing to know what it is.

The same expression reads the real trigger and the test node, because the test node is shaped exactly like Outlook's output. onError continues so a dead API routes to a human rather than failing the run -- the error shape has no `proceed`, so the IF sends it down the false branch.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ output: $json.output || '', subject: $('Prepare').item.json.subject || '', conversation_id: $('Prepare').item.json.conversation_id, format: $('Prepare').item.json.format, exchange_id: $('Prepare').item.json.exchange_id, searched: ($json.intermediateSteps || []).length > 0 }) }}

nodes.name: Finalize
nodes.notes:
Everything decidable once the answer exists: was it grounded, and what does the draft read like.

Both halves used to live in this canvas -- the refusal test as two regexes inside an IF condition, the greeting and sign-off as string concatenation in a Code node. Both were copies of rag.core, and a copied safety check is one that will eventually disagree with itself. They are now one implementation, covered by scripts/rag_eval.py.

The refusal test is deliberately two nets: the NOT_IN_DOCUMENTS token leaks. Measured on seven unanswerable questions the 9B emitted the token for four and answered the other three in prose -- 'the provided documentation does not specify how many days' -- a well-formed answer that says nothing. `reason` distinguishes them, so you can tell a corpus gap from a model that will not say so.

The shell is assembled here and never by the model. Retrieval grounds the factual body; letting the model write the courtesy around it reopens the gap it was stopped from filling ('we look forward to seeing you at our campus').

`searched` tells the API whether the agent called academy_docs at all (intermediateSteps is non-empty). A reply written with no search is never grounded -- the model skipped the tool and answered from its own head -- so it goes to Human queue with reason 'the agent answered without searching the documents'. Needs 'Return Intermediate Steps' switched on in the AI Agent node.

nodes.name: Wait for review
nodes.notes: Holds the execution open until a human approves on /review and clicks Send -- review_send() in api.py POSTs the final reply to $execution.resumeUrl (captured by Queue for review (UI), previous node), and the two nodes after it run on that text: Record final draft, then Outlook Draft. Resume = On Webhook Call (POST), capped at 14 days (limitWaitTime/resumeAmount): past that the execution resumes with no body and the reply can no longer be drafted from /review. Respond = When Last Node Finishes: the API's Send call gets its answer only after both have run, so a failed draft is reported to the reviewer (the reply itself is recorded either way). NOTE: with empty parameters this node defaults to a 5-second timer and does not wait at all.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ reply: $('Wait for review').item.json.body.reply, attachment_name: ($('Wait for review').item.json.body.attachment || {}).name || null }) }}

nodes.name: Record final draft
nodes.notes: Records the reviewer's final text (from the Wait node) and marks the row sent on /review, via /review/{id}/drafted. It does NOT depend on Outlook Draft: it sits above it on the canvas, n8n runs the branches after the Wait top to bottom, so this runs first and the reply is recorded whether or not the draft could be created. A failed draft is reported to the reviewer as a warning on the review page.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify(Object.assign({ comment: $json.body.reply }, $json.body.attachment ? { message: { attachments: [{ '@odata.type': '#microsoft.graph.fileAttachment', name: $json.body.attachment.name, contentType: $json.body.attachment.content_type, contentBytes: $json.body.attachment.content_b64 }] } } : {})) }}

nodes.name: Outlook Draft
nodes.notes:
Runs when the reviewer clicks Send on /review: the Wait node's output is the JSON the API posted -- { exchange_id, reply, ref, subject } -- and this turns `reply` into a reply DRAFT in the mailbox, threaded on the original (`ref`) with the original quoted beneath. A person opens it in Outlook and presses Send. Nothing in this workflow sends mail.

createReply through the Microsoft Outlook OAuth2 credential the trigger uses (needs Mail.ReadWrite) -- not the Outlook node's Message > Reply operation, which sends immediately unless its 'Save as Draft' option is on.

Keep this the LOWEST node after the Wait: it is the one that can fail, and a failure stops the execution, so anything placed below it would not run.

If the reviewer attached a file on /review it arrives as `attachment` { name, content_type, content_b64 } and is added to the draft in the same call (under 3 MB; the API enforces the limit).

nodes.name: Queue for manual reply (UI)
nodes.notes: The Human queue is no longer a dead end. An email the documents could not answer is put on the review page's Manual replies tab (/review#manual) with NO AI reply: a person writes the reply there and clicks Send. From then on it is the same path as a reviewed reply -- this execution waits at Wait for review, and Record final draft and Outlook Draft run on the text the person wrote. The API also adds that hand-written reply to the knowledge base, so the next enquiry on the same point can be answered from it.
